description: Core-seeded interval/range predicates anchored on std/core.mm bounds primitives. Each atom is a structural 0/1 witness or bounded-safe difference over closed integer intervals [lo, hi], useful for downstream container range checks and scheduling/overlap logic. All bodies are explicit linear integer constraints with 0/1 witnesses, remaining entirely within the Z3 decidable fragment (no multiplication of two variables, no division, no quantifiers).
implementation_notes: Each atom has an explicit body so deterministic forge rendering never needs an LLM credential.
Use only linear integer constraints and 0/1 witnesses; interval endpoints are closed (inclusive).
Anchor the contracts on std/core.mm bounds concepts (safe_to_index) and reuse the std/core_guards is_in_bounds convention without importing new trusted atoms.

atoms.name: ranges_disjoint
atoms.description: Return a 0/1 witness for whether the closed intervals [a_lo, a_hi] and [b_lo, b_hi] do not overlap.
atoms.body: if a_hi < b_lo { 1 } else { if b_hi < a_lo { 1 } else { 0 } }

atoms.name: ranges_overlap
atoms.description: Return a 0/1 witness for whether the closed intervals [a_lo, a_hi] and [b_lo, b_hi] share at least one point.
atoms.body: if a_hi < b_lo { 0 } else { if b_hi < a_lo { 0 } else { 1 } }

atoms.name: range_width_nonneg
atoms.description: Return the non-negative width of a non-negative closed interval [lo, hi].

atoms.name: point_before_range
atoms.description: Return a 0/1 witness for whether point p lies strictly below the closed interval [lo, hi].
